validity.recommendation: reclassify PipelineType as distribution [BAIRD RULING 2026-09-15] APPROVED AS STAGED. A distribution project may stay in GGIT so long as PipelineType says 'distribution' -- the correction is the fix, not a reason to remove the row. No existence or scope action owed.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence and duplicate checks both come back clean, and this row DOES involve new physical pipe (not a compression-only expansion like P7790/P7812 elsewhere in this batch). Southwest Gas Corporation's June 12, 2019 filing at the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada (PUCN), 'Application ... for Authority to Expand Natural Gas Service Pursuant to Nevada Revised Statutes 704.9925,' establishes the sponsor (Southwest Gas Corp), state (Nevada, Elko County/Spring Creek) and statutory basis before any name-collision risk was entertained -- this is the same document the sheet's PipelineType [ref] already cites (existing_ref_checks show name_found=true on it), so no thin same-name match is in play. Confirmed live in 24 consecutive EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects releases (2019-07 through 2026-08, project_key 'spring creek gas infrastructure expansion project|southwest gas') and on Southwest Gas's own live project microsite springcreekgas.com. No duplicate in the 42-row roster: distinct from Great Basin Gas Transmission Company (P7856-P7860), a separate FERC-regulated interstate subsidiary of the same parent (Southwest Gas Holdings) -- not the same physical line as this LDC service-territory expansion. CLASSIFICATION CONCERN: the sheet's PipelineType is 'transmission', but the applicant's own filing calls both components of the project 'distribution' pipe throughout: Sec.4.2 -- the 12.1-mile 8-inch steel approach main is described as 'high pressure steel distribution pipeline'; Sec.4.3 -- the 168-mile PE network is the 'Distribution System.' The 22-mile PE run this row's LengthKnown tracks (matches EIA's notes field verbatim, '22-mile backbone with 168 miles of distribution pipeline') is itself customer-facing PE main built 'to serve the schools, businesses and residences along the route' -- an LDC main extension under NRS 704.9925, not an interstate/intrastate transmission trunk. GEM's own controlled vocabulary lists 'distribution' as a valid PipelineType (separate from 'transmission' and 'gathering'; controlled_vocab.md line 18), so this is a real reclassification candidate, not a vocabulary gap. Only the applicant's own filing states this directly (medium-strength single origin for the classification claim specifically); EIA's own 'Pipeline Type' field for this project reads 'Intrastate' (a jurisdictional label, not a pipe-type value, so it neither confirms nor contradicts). Tier below reflects the existence finding (2 independent origins) and the classification recommendation is corroborated only by the primary filing -- see the PipelineType fill for the matching correction. [BAIRD RULING 2026-09-15] APPROVED AS STAGED. A distribution project may stay in GGIT so long as PipelineType says 'distribution' -- the correction is the fix, not a reason to remove the row. No existence or scope action owed.

Searched the 2019 PUCN application (all exhibits/testimony, full text) and the EIA Aug2026 release for a throughput/design-day capacity figure (MMcf/d or dekatherms/day) specific to this Backbone segment -- found none. The filing discusses peak-day demand and customer growth projections in aggregate for the whole service territory, not a segment capacity number. EIA's own Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) column for this project is blank in every one of its 24 releases (2019-07 through 2026-08). Genuinely nothing found; left UNRESOLVED rather than force a number.

The application states the SEPARATE 12.1-mile steel approach main is 'high pressure' (qualitative only, no MAOP/psig figure) -- and that segment is not the one this row's LengthKnown (22 mi) tracks. No numeric operating pressure is stated anywhere in the filing for the 22-mile PE backbone segment itself, and NPMS/PHMSA time did not permit a segment-specific pull within this pass. Left UNRESOLVED.

The filing gives a diameter (8-inch) only for the separate 12.1-mile steel approach main, which is NOT the segment this row's LengthKnown (22 mi PE) tracks -- citing 8-inch here would be an aggregate/wrong-segment mismatch (the approach main isn't its own PID in this roster). FuelSource wants the upstream field/plant/facility feeding the line (gem_schema.md), not a fuel type. EIA's notes name the system's upstream interconnects -- 'connecting to the Ruby and Paiute pipelines' -- but those are interstate TRANSMISSION PIPELINES, not a named gas field or plant, so I did not force-fit them into this field per the schema's 'do not default it' instruction. Flagging the Ruby/Paiute interconnects here for a reviewer's judgment call rather than staging them as FuelSource. Left UNRESOLVED.

summary: Spring Creek Gas Infrastructure Expansion Project (P7823): real, single-owner Southwest Gas LDC main-extension project in Elko County, NV, genuinely under construction with new physical pipe (not compression-only); reclassify PipelineType transmission->distribution per the applicant's own filing (validity concern); 9 REFS_ADDED/REVERIFIED units at high or medium tier (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Proposal, Construction, Start, Length, Location, SegmentCost, Operator, Owner all now properly sourced off the dated EIA release + the 2019 PUCN application, replacing the data.php navigation-page refs); 4 UNRESOLVED (Capacity, Pressure, Diameter, FuelSource -- none found in the filing or EIA at this segment's scope); status review verdict=confirm, evidence 2026-08.
